question: Levonorgestrel-only emergency contraception (the 'morning-after pill') is effective if taken within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse, with efficacy declining the longer the delay.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The 72-hour window is the licensed indication for levonorgestrel EC. Beyond 72 hours, ulipristal acetate (120 h window) or a copper IUD (5-day window, most effective) are preferred.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! Levonorgestrel EC is most effective within 24 hours (~95% effective) and retains some efficacy up to 72 hours (~58%). Ulipristal acetate extends the window to 120 hours.
